:::{#exm-poisson-log-partition-mean}
#### The mean of the Poisson distribution from its log-partition function

<!-- no-figure: the example compares two numbers computed from the same data -->

In @exm-poisson-exponential-family,
the [statistic](sufficiency.qmd#def-statistic) is $\statf{\rvar} = \rvar$
and the log-partition function is $\logpartitionf{\natparam} = \expf{\natparam}$.
By @thm-log-partition-mean,

$$
\E{\Rvar}
= \E{\statf{\Rvar}}
= \dif{\logpartitionf{\natparam}}{\natparam}
= \expf{\natparam}.
$$

Since $\expf{\natparam} = \rate$,
the derivative is the [mean](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-expectation) of the
[Poisson distribution](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-poisson), $\rate$.
For the cyclone data, the [derivative](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-derivatives.html#def-derivative) at the
[natural parameter](#def-natural-parameter) $\natparam = `r round(natural_parameter, 3)`$ is
$\expf{\natparam} = `r round(exp(natural_parameter), 3)`$,
which equals the [sample mean](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-sample-mean) `r round(mean(cyclones), 3)`.
:::
